ops.title: FinalizeAdd id-reservation window: ConsumeAccountIndex before UpsertAccount
ops.description:
`internal/pool/account.go` `FinalizeAdd` (~line 287): `ConsumeAccountIndex` (DELETE from `pending_adds`) runs as a separate SQL statement BEFORE `UpsertAccount` (INSERT into `accounts`). For that window an account id is absent from BOTH `pending_adds` and `accounts`, so `ReserveAccountIndex` (`MIN candidate NOT IN accounts UNION pending_adds`) can re-hand the same id to a concurrent `ccp add`/materialize → two writers collide on one row / config dir / Keychain service name.

**Provenance:** surfaced by the cred-sync-origin re-verify (codex finding, fable-confirmed real) but OUT of the 11-commit sync fix diff — `account.go` last changed in 54165ded/2c1411ed/77f03928, none in that range. Does NOT undermine the sync fix pass: FIX 8's `installEnvelope` per-account lock is a different critical section, held while the id is still reserved in `pending_adds`; this race is the later `FinalizeAdd` consume→upsert phase. Likelihood is very low (a concurrent reserve must land in the two-statement microsecond window).

**Fix:** make `ConsumeAccountIndex` + `UpsertAccount` atomic — a single store transaction, or reorder to upsert-then-consume with a `RowsAffected != 1` collision check — so an id is never simultaneously absent from both tables.

ops.text: FinalizeAdd never leaves an account id absent from both pending_adds and accounts: ConsumeAccountIndex and UpsertAccount execute in one transaction, or upsert precedes consume with a RowsAffected!=1 collision guard
A test exercises a concurrent ReserveAccountIndex racing FinalizeAdd's consume->upsert window and asserts the same id is never handed out twice
